title: Statistics Adventure 1: Averages & Range
welcome_lead: Time to make sense of data! You'll learn the three averages, find the range, and spot the difference between discrete and continuous data.
meta_desc: GCSE Maths Statistics walkthrough — mean, median, mode, range from a list, and discrete vs continuous data.
final_note: You learned mean, median, mode and range from a list — plus how to tell discrete data from continuous data.

walkthroughs.body_html:
An average is a single value that represents a whole set of data.

There are three to know:

  • Mean — add up all values and divide by how many.
  • Median — sort the data, then pick the middle one.
  • Mode — the value that appears most often.

Tip: always sort the data first before finding the median!

The range tells you how spread out your data is.

Range = largest − smallest

Example: for 4, 7, 9, 12 the range is 12 − 4 = 8.

A small range means values are close together. A big range means they are spread far apart.

Discrete data can only take certain values — usually whole numbers you can count. Like the number of goals in a match.

Continuous data can take any value in a range. Like height, weight or time — you can always measure more precisely.

Quick test: ask 'can it be 3.74?' If yes, it's continuous!

mcqs.q: Which average is the MIDDLE value when the data is in order?
options: Mean
Median
Mode
Range

mcqs.q: Which of these is CONTINUOUS data?
options: Number of pets owned
Shoe sizes
Height of a tree
Number of siblings

mcqs.q: Which average is best to use for the data set [2, 3, 3, 4, 4, 4, 5, 100]?
options: The mean — it always gives the most accurate average.
5, because that is the middle value.
The median (3.5) — it isn't distorted by the outlier 100, unlike the mean.
The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: The mode, because the most common value is always the best representative.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.
5, because that is the middle value.
7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
5, because that is the middle value.
